title: Minor Hall and Baby Dodds swap: Oliver fined by the union
summary: Oliver dismissed drummer Minor Hall without notice, sent for Baby Dodds without union permission, and the union fined him $200.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Was that when Minor Hall and Baby Dolls changed places?

They changed places in, uh, Oakland. I mean, in Frisco. He fired Jimmy Pilar. He said, oh. He didn't give him a notice. He didn't give him no notice. And Ram told him, he says, why, uh, why you want to let this boy go? Where's the end of the Southern Pacific line out there? Going to this cold ticket, let a man go and you ain't give him no notice or nothing?
He said, well, uh, he's entitled to notice. He said, notice. He didn't give him his five bucks. I ain't give him nothing.
He said, well, I'll quit too. Jimmy, go, I'll go too.

Yeah. That was great. He sent for Baby Dolls in St. Louis. He don't consult with the board. You see, when you get ready to send somebody, you got to go consult with the board. At the union? The union. Get the permission to send for a man. He don't know if the man's in good standing or not. He sent for him. The boy come and he was in bad standing in St. Louis. The boy comes, a man goes on down to number six. I go with him, I don't know what happened. Then they had us all to come on up to number six. And they found out that this boy wasn't bad standing in the union. So the financial. They fined Joe $200. They asked Joe, didn't even know he was doing the wrong in both of drummer and he helped out consulting with the board. I don't know. He said, you don't know if we could get your drummer. Well, you ain't got no drummer that'll fit in with my band. He said, that's up to us. To find out if they had one and if not, you could have got a drummer from any place you want. As long as you get permission from us, you run over our head. Well, they found him $200 and he had to pay. He had to use this boy two more weeks. See? Boy had to work on a two weeks notice and Ram had to, Ram had to say, Ram said, I want to work. I told him. He said, you have to give him a two weeks notice. Huh? See? So Ram had to stay two weeks and Jim had to stay a week, two weeks and he had to give him transportation to go back to Chicago. Yeah, he got laid. So he had to follow him for $200. All right, he got ready to go. He left there and he paid that money, all that money. He gets back to Heath and goes back to New York and goes back to Chicago and goes to Oakland No, Royal Garden, again. That woman was running that place. They found everybody worked with you.
